answer_1.quote: In our experimental setup, we aim to automatically transform raw versions of FAQ help pages into polished, easily readable texts for customers.

answer_2.quote: First we analyzed the generated texts using ROUGE, a traditional n-gram-based text similarity metric, and BERTScore, a metric relying on dense vector embeddings to approximate the semantic similarity between generated text and the groundtruth.

answer_3.quote: We followed the work of and utilized GPT-4 to score the output texts on a Likert scale of 1-5 stars using the evaluation prompts listed in Table.
methods: evaluation prompts for hallucinations, informativeness, coherence

answer_4.quote: In addition to automated assessments, we conducted a manual evaluation of helpfulness of the category input text generated text by expert editors of DT.
answer_4.guideline: The editors were prompted to address the following three questions: 1. Which reformulation of the input is superior: Version 1 or Version 2? 2. On a scale, how much revision would be necessary for the better of the two suggestions to render an acceptable text? 3. Would the superior suggestion aid your work (e.g., save time)?
